description.value: A longitudinal two-center resting-state fMRI study investigated functional connectivity differences and changes over 1.8 years in patients with Alzheimer's disease, behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia, and control participants.
Longitudinal observational study conducted at two dementia centers, with MRI and neuropsychological assessment at baseline and follow-up.

value: At baseline, patients with AD showed higher functional connectivity than controls between the lingual gyrus and the medial visual network, between the central opercular gyrus and the auditory system network, between the paracingulate gyrus and the executive control network, and between the paracingulate gyrus and the salience network.
AD patients also showed lower mean connectivity in the right and left frontoparietal networks compared with controls.

spans.text: The results of post hoc testing showed higher functional connectivity in AD compared with controls between the lingual gyrus and network I (medial visual network), between the central opercular gyrus and network III (auditory system network), between the paracingulate gyrus and network VI (executive control network), and between the paracingulate gyrus and network IX (salience network) (Fig. 4A, AD > HC, yellow-to-red voxels, Table 2).

In a final analysis, we investigated the possible associations between changes in network-to-region connectivity and longitudinal changes in cognitive performance (i.e., Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) score [48] and Frontal Assessment Battery (FAB) scores [49]), using linear regression analyses (IBM SPSS Statistics Version 20, IBM Corp.
It has been suggested that testing multiple cognitive domains is required to differentiate both types of dementia rather than focus on one cognitive test [63].

description.value: The Mini-Mental State Examination was administered as a measure of global cognitive status. MMSE scores were used to characterize cognitive performance and assess longitudinal change; Alzheimer’s disease patients showed a significant decline at follow-up.

spans.text: Patients with AD performed worse at follow-up compared with baseline on MMSE (p = 0.016)

description.value: The Frontal Assessment Battery was administered as a measure of executive functioning. FAB scores were used to characterize cognitive performance and assess longitudinal change.

spans.text: Changes in FAB scores were not associated with changes in supramarginal (p = 0.310) and inferior frontal gyrus (p = 0.694) connectivity in bvFTD.
